scope: Production two-wide fetched CSR/MRET/WFI, precise traps including ECALL/EBREAK and accepted redirects with one shared CSR bank. No LSU, interrupts, predictor, full architectural suite or physical timing claim.
drain: drained_i remains externally coordinated: enable_i low, no offered/accepted instruction transaction or buffered frontend token, empty backend and no held producers or other identity holders. For generation exhaustion the caller must preserve the committed restart PC, drain outstanding fetch traffic and the backend, flush buffered fetch state with external restart, then pulse drained_i while enable remains low. This top does not automate drain or silently wrap ROB generations.
dispatch: CSR/MRET/WFI are supported only with TRAP_SERVICE=1. They allocate alone through head_system_dispatch, preserve full ROB identity and renamed source (including rd=rs1), bypass IQ, and block all younger allocation until actual retirement or recovery. Older IQ work remains enabled. Unsupported memory/FENCE operations retain their existing stall behavior.
ownership: At the matching head, the descriptor reserves PRF reads, suppresses IQ issue and waits for read readiness. The shared head controller freezes the response. Legal acceptance atomically updates CSR state, PRF/committed ownership, ROB order and minstret. Normal CSR acceptance does not redirect; MRET redirects on its accepted retirement edge. No same-edge younger allocation occurs.
illegal: Illegal CSR accesses offer a resultless cause-2 completion on port zero, qualified by completion_enable_i[0]. Ordinary producer completions are held during that arbitration. The descriptor remains until the resulting trap is accepted. Final trap acceptance applies CSR effects, clears ROB/IQ/producers/descriptor and redirects to current mtvec.
recovery: External flush/reset/fatal cancel pending system responses. Accepted older branch recovery discards an unprepared younger descriptor. A pending head response or raw head fault blocks branch resolution, avoiding accepted-recovery feedback through CSR acceptance. Frontend redirect transport preserves offered requests and drains accepted stale responses. Global drain requires all existing holders plus the system descriptor/controller to be empty.
verification: The shared fetch reference checks all architectural event bits, register dependencies, fetched instructions and memory handshakes. At observed system_prepare_o it requires the next architectural instruction to be CSR/MRET/WFI, with no earlier prepared response or concurrent retirement, then independently computes expected effects from architectural GPR/CSR state. This handshake provides the sampling cycle for changing counter CSRs; result data, operand tags, CSR effects and accepted state are not copied from the DUT. CSR counters advance independently each cycle and all accepted events update the reference. system_busy_o is observable response occupancy. Directed/random programs cover all CSR forms, x0/immediates/rd=rs1, illegal CSR trap-return, programmable mtvec/mepc, MRET with stale fetch traffic, stalls, branch kills and cancellation. ECALL/EBREAK cover both lanes and all eight instruction-line offsets, exact handler mcause/mtval/mepc reads, and MRET to the following instruction; the shared counter model checks that trap acceptance does not increment minstret.
environment: With FRONTEND_FAULTS=1, exact ECALL/EBREAK encodings use source/destination-free ROB/IQ fault tokens. ECALL saves cause 11 and mtval=0; EBREAK saves cause 3 and mtval=faulting PC. Fetch faults retain priority. A lane-zero fault ends the accepted prefix; a lane-one fault can accompany older work. Only head trap acceptance updates the shared CSR bank and redirects to mtvec; neither instruction retires nor increments minstret. Wrong-path faults are discarded by older recovery. Reserved neighboring encodings remain illegal instruction traps.
wfi: Exact WFI is an immediate-resume serialized hint. It allocates solo, blocks younger dispatch, waits for all older work and head preparation, then retires alone with PC+4, no redirect, no GPR write and no explicit CSR effect. minstret counts accepted WFI once unless inhibited. Held responses and reset/flush/fatal or older-branch cancellation follow the existing system path. FENCE and FENCE.I remain unsupported until memory ordering and instruction visibility are implemented. The benches use unsupported FENCE as a stopping marker; they do not claim fence execution.
